sections.title: What Is Machine Learning?
rules: To solve a problem on a computer, you need an algorithm.
An algorithm is a sequence of instructions that transforms input data into output data.
For some tasks, we know the exact algorithm (for example, sorting numbers).
For other tasks, we do not know the algorithm. An example is spam email detection.
We know the input: an email message.
We know the output: a decision (spam or not spam).
We do not know how to write explicit rules to transform the input into the output.
In machine learning, we use example data to fill this knowledge gap.
We collect thousands of sample emails.
We let the computer extract the algorithm from the data.
In large databases, finding useful models from data is called data mining.
Machine learning is also a branch of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
An intelligent system must adapt when the environment changes.
Machine learning helps solve problems in vision, speech recognition, and robotics.
Machine learning is programming computers to optimize a performance criterion with example data or past experience.
The model can be predictive (make predictions for new data) or descriptive (gain knowledge from data).

sections.title: Examples of Machine Learning Applications
rules: Learning Associations: In retail, basket analysis finds items that customers buy together.
If a customer buys product X, calculate conditional probability P(Y|X) to find if they buy Y.
Classification: In credit scoring, calculate risk to predict whether a customer will default.
The input is customer information (income, savings). The output is class: low-risk or high-risk.
A discriminant function separates the examples of different classes.
Regression: Predict a continuous numeric value (for example, used car price from mileage).
Both classification and regression are supervised learning problems.
Unsupervised Learning: There is no supervisor. We find regularities and structure in input data.
Clustering groups similar inputs together for customer segmentation or image compression.
Reinforcement Learning: The system outputs a sequence of actions called a policy.
The system receives delayed rewards and learns past good action sequences.

sections.title: Notes & Foundations
rules: Humans learn from experience to adapt to changing environments.
Science is model fitting: Scientists make observations and infer general rules (induction).
Statistics provides the mathematical framework for parameter estimation.
Computer science provides efficient algorithms for optimization and inference.
